course_name_original: Fisica tecnica ed elementi di trasmissione del calore
course_name_en: Technical Physics and Heat Transfer Elements

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with fundamental knowledge of applied Thermodynamics necessary for the analysis of processes and systems involving energy transformations and/or energy transfers and heat transfer.
Emphasize energy conversion and its limits, as well as criteria for thermodynamic optimization of processes and systems.
Analyze the three fundamental mechanisms of heat exchange: one-dimensional conduction, convection, and radiation.

Provide students with tools to evaluate the thermodynamic performance of main components of energy conversion systems (thermal engines and operators) and to assess the power exchanged in the three heat transfer mechanisms considered individually and in combination.
Knowledge of issues related to energy conversions and energy exchanges according to the three mechanisms (conduction, convection, and radiation).
Identify the limits of energy conversions, the efficiency of systems, and the potential for heat exchange of the three heat transfer mechanisms.
Identify and compare different problem-solving methodologies.
Collaborate within a working group, defining objectives, activities, and tools.
Reflect on the knowledge and skills of their educational path, identify possibilities for further development of knowledge, abilities, and competences.

syllabus_topics: Concepts and basic definitions (0.5 CFU): system and environment, properties, state, equation of state, pure substance, phase, simple compressible system, classical and continuum thermodynamics, thermodynamic and local equilibrium, quasi-static process and transformation, energy, work, heat, temperature.

First and second law of thermodynamics for closed systems (2 CFU): first law for isolated and closed system, first law as a balance equation, enthalpy and differential forms of the first law for a closed system. Postulate on entropy and its consequences: evolution of an isolated system by removing internal constraints, the entropy postulate, reversible transformations and second law for an isolated system, Gibbs equations, second law for a control mass, Clausius inequality, volume change work, state postulate, specific heats, p-v, T-s thermodynamic planes, second law and energy conversion systems.
Formulation of general laws for the study of open systems (0.5 CFU): generalities, mass continuity equation, first and second law of thermodynamics for open systems. Mechanical energy equation.

Thermodynamics of states (1 CFU): introduction, characteristic surface, diagrams: pressure-temperature, pressure-volume, temperature-entropy, enthalpy-entropy, pressure-enthalpy, ideal gases, internally reversible adiabatic transformation, and polytropic, liquids, saturated and superheated vapors.
Components of thermodynamic systems (1 CFU): conduit, generalities on dynamic fluid machines, steam turbine, pump, compressor, thermal power transfer components, throttling valve.

Humid air (1 CFU): Dalton's Law. Properties: specific and relative humidity, dew point, adiabatic saturation, dry bulb and wet bulb temperature, enthalpy, specific volume. Psychrometric chart. Elementary transformations: heating, simple cooling and with dehumidification, adiabatic mixing, adiabatic humidification.
Generalities on heat transfer: General and particular laws. Statements of Fourier, Planck and Newton's laws.

Conduction (2 CFU): Fundamental constitutive relation for conduction. Differential equation of conduction. Boundary conditions. Adimensionalization. One-dimensional steady state: planar symmetry, total thermal resistance for walls in series and parallel, cylindrical and spherical symmetry with and without internal generation. One-dimensional unsteady state: Biot > 0.10 and Biot < 0.10.

Radiation (2 CFU): Generalities. Emissive power, radiosity, irradiation, absorption, reflection, transmission coefficients. Black body: definition and properties. Emission characteristics: Stefan-Boltzmann's Law, Planck's Law, Wien's Law. Radiative characteristics of surfaces: spectral and total emittance for real and gray body. Kirchhoff's Law. Definition of configuration factors. Radiative heat exchange between parallel and indefinite plane surfaces: black and gray surfaces. Radiative heat exchange in cavities. Radiative screens. Solar and atmospheric radiation.

Convection (2 CFU): Laminar and turbulent flow. Dynamic and kinematic viscosity. Adimensionalization. Forced convection: dimensionless groups, thermal and dynamic boundary layer, for external and internal flow. Pressure losses. Natural convection: dimensionless groups. Relations for evaluating the average unit convective conductance in natural and forced convection.
teaching_methods: Practice exercises in classroom with support from professor and tutors
Demonstrations using whiteboard (digital or real) for Technical Physics
Use of slides for Heat Transfer part (available on Moodle)
Provision of exercise material (tracks, tables, diagrams)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test, held jointly. The written test is graded in bands: A (28-30), B (25-27), C (22-24), D (18-21). Students who do not achieve the minimum required value (D) in the written test are rejected and must repeat it in another session. Access to the oral exam is conditional on passing the written exam. Both tests contribute equally to the final grade. Failure to attend or pass the oral exam results in rejection, requiring the student to repeat the written exam in another session.
